newsitem.title: USA: Sweet crude grade prices rachet higher in US Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Sweet crude grade prices rachet higher in US Gulf.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices gained Friday morning, tracking technical advances established in the futures sector, while cash grades featured firming sweet crude differentials.
August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was 20-25 cents stronger at $19.30-40 a barrel, around 10 cents weaker than second month September benchmark WTI/Cushing crude.
The performance in the sweet grade market allowed Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James to trade at a 20 cents premium to the August marker, around 10 cents higher than Thursday.
Traders said the fact no North Sea Brent crude was fixed to the U.S. Gulf gave the domestic sweets a boost.
"People don't see Brent fixtures, so they're picking-up domestic pipeline batches, holding up the sweet a little bit," said the trader.
Secondary reasons for the firmer LLS/St. James included refiners buying-up crude ahead of possible hurricane season outages in the Gulf, traders said.
For the other markets, West Texas Sour/Midland sold at $1.25 under August WTI/Cushing, and Eugene Island at a $1.40 discount to the same marker.
Rumors of a Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire deal at -25 cents to WTI/Cushing were also making the rounds, traders said.
August Exchange for Physicals quietly tracked around a 3-4 cents premium to the cash, but their attractiveness continued to fade with the alleviation of the foreign crude overhang in the Gulf.
